string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of its four direct-administered municipalities, located in the country\'s north. With a recorded history of more than three thousand years, it served as the imperial capital for the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. The city is home to landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall at Badaling, the Temple of Heaven, and the Summer Palace. As the national political, cultural, and educational centre, Beijing hosts the headquarters of major state institutions and many leading universities. It became the first city to host both the Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Olympic Games.

Shanghai is China\'s largest city and a global financial centre, situated on the country\'s central eastern coast at the mouth of the Yangtze River. Originally a small fishing and trading town, it grew into an international treaty port in the nineteenth century. Today its skyline is defined by the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Shanghai Tower in the Lujiazui financial district, while the Bund preserves rows of colonial-era buildings. Shanghai is a national hub for finance, trade, shipping, manufacturing, and technology, and it contributes a substantial share of China\'s foreign trade and industrial output.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwestern China, located at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. Built on steep hills and surrounded by mountains, it is famous for its layered, three-dimensional cityscape, dense river-crossing bridges, and foggy winters. Historically, Chongqing served as the temporary capital of China during the Second Sino-Japanese War. Today it is a major inland industrial, manufacturing, and transportation hub, and a key city on the Yangtze River Economic Belt. It is also widely known for its fiery spicy hotpot cuisine.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, lying on the coast of the Bohai Sea about 120 kilometres southeast of Beijing. Historically a major northern treaty port and commercial centre, it preserves a mix of Chinese and European colonial architecture, including the restored Italian-style concession. The city is known for the Tianjin Eye, a Ferris wheel built across the Hai River, and for local snacks such as Goubuli steamed buns and fried mahua dough twists. Tianjin is a leading port, industrial, and educational centre, and forms part of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei economic cluster.
